name: The log jail's plank palisade

documented_range.note: Continuity bounds copied from the enclosed jail phase, not a dated fence contract. Gale1902 p51 remembers the small jail concealed within a high plank palisade in his1835 town-walk narrative; its exact completion relative to1July is not dated. The separate plate is captioned1836. Building this enclosure in theJuly scene is a declared continuity reconstruction; neither the1833 opening bound nor the1835 closing bound dates this fence.

existence.note: Gale1902 p51 explicitly places the small log jail within a high plank palisade, with John Beach occupying a house partly within the same enclosure facingRandolph. This retrospective1835-framed narrative supports the palisade kind and existence, not a measured layout or exactJuly condition. The1836-captioned plate is a later depicted state, not contemporary corroboration.

runs.note: ONE V4 R compound outline, not a traced/surveyed ground plan. The continuous north high-plank face is7.496 m long; this is ENCLOSURE length, not a change to the unchanged6.096 x4.572 m log core. The core moves1.30 m south only. Retain0.70 m west and rear core clearance; the former east divider is removed so a low keeper-link gate can connect the tall NE endpoint to the keeper NW corner. Rear closure reaches2.00 m into the6.40 m keeper back wall so part of the keeper is topologically inside the compound, consistent with Gale wording but not a measured plan. That2.00 m attachment and the exact outline are reconstructed. No tall fence crosses the native core doorway zone. Keeper/source-camera inputs stay V3.

fence_type.note: Gale calls it a high PLANK PALISADE. The independently verified1902 plate shows close-set vertical boards or pales enclosing the jail. The existing closed-board construction is used with its optional pointed heads, read from that plate; exact stock and dimensions remain reconstructed.

height_m.note: Chosen10ft(3.05m, rounded), not a source measurement. Bound by the text concealed within a HIGH palisade and the unchanged2.66m jail eaves: a normal6ft yard fence would expose most of those walls. The current12degree core roof remains unresolved, so this height is not fitted to its ridge or claimed as an1835 dimension. SUPERSEDED HEIGHT TRIAL 2026-11-09 (T-2380): use 8 ft (2.44 m, rounded) rather than the earlier 10 ft choice. Both retrospective pictures show a roof or cap of the jail itself above the palisade, while the former 3.05 m enclosure concealed almost all of the retained 2.66 m-eave/12-degree core in the Gale comparison. This lower, still-high enclosure is a reconstructed relative-exposure choice, not a measurement from either drawing. It leaves the existing core, keeper, all endpoints, board stock, gate and confidence grades unchanged. The chosen relation keeps the core walls largely hidden while allowing the roof above the fence; fresh picture review is still required, and neither the conflicting core-roof identity nor exact July1835 continuity is resolved.

rail_courses.note: Three backing stringers support the tall closed boards. No source counts them; the existing board-fence construction is reused.

post_spacing_m.note: Chosen8ft backing-post bays, copied from the existing boarded yard construction, not measured in the plate.

post_size_m.note: Chosen180mm square posts for a tall closure, not a source scantling.

board_width_m.note: Chosen10in wide boards, using the existing boarded-yard stock. No pictorial width is promoted to a measured dimension.

board_gap_m.note: Chosen6mm shrinkage gap so the palisade reads as a closed enclosure rather than an open garden fence. Not a measured gap.

top_shape.note: The complete1902 Trowbridge plate clearly shows pointed tops along the high palisade. Use the native optional pointed pale top, not jagged or randomly varied boards. Its exact angle and rise are reconstructed.

point_height_m.note: Half the chosen254mm board width gives a127mm symmetrical pointed head. The revised total fence height2.44m includes this same head; backing posts stop at the2.313m shoulder. No source measures the cut angle or point height. Only the overall reconstructed height is revised in the 2026-11-09 exposure trial; board width, gap, thickness and point rise are retained.

citations.citation: Edwin O.Gale, Reminiscences of Early Chicago and Vicinity (Chicago:Fleming H.Revell,1902), p51 and plate facingp53; actual scan n76/n79. Illustration byW.E.S.Trowbridge, captioned1836.
citations.tier_label: retrospective memoir and illustration, independently verified1902 publication

research_note:
The high pointed plank enclosure now includes the separate keeper component and a continuous front. The old reconstructed central entrance gap is replaced by a low house-side hung gate in log_jail_keeper_link; the unchanged core door is behind the high front with its own reconstructed approach setback. The Gale1836-captioned picture and1835-framed narrative support the kind and partly enclosed house relation, not these numeric bounds or exactJuly1835continuity. Core roof/relative compound proportions remain DIFFERS. Actual current published terrain, both doorway approaches and gate clearance are still required before release acceptance.

2026-11-09 T-2380 relative-exposure trial: reduce only the reconstructed overall palisade height from3.05m to2.44m(8ft, rounded), so the retained core roof can read above it as both retrospective drawings show. This is not a historic measured fence height, a resolved core-roof reconstruction, a new July1835 date, a paint/colour decision or a new board-stock feature. Native separate254mm boards/6mm gaps/pointedheads were already present. No enclosure endpoint, doorway approach, low hung gate or building input moves. Fresh source/current comparisons and published view inspection remain pending.
